fatal_errors: The proposed deposited RHEA interlayer is not the target intervention, which was liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu to create aligned, bicontinuous Cu channels and retained RHEA ligaments.

The cited evidence supports irradiation tolerance and thermal stability of a different nanocrystalline RHEA, but does not establish that an RHEA coating lowers W–Cu thermal boundary resistance or increases composite thermal conductivity.

Mechanical durability and fusion-relevant irradiation resistance of the finished coated composite are asserted without direct supporting evidence; the target study itself only used low-energy He implantation of precursor dendrites as a proxy and did not establish composite mechanical strength.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested W–Cu thermal/irradiation tradeoff and provides a controlled, falsifiable comparison, so it is a coherent alternative concept. However, it does not reconstruct the reported materials strategy. The target used 1200 °C, 96 h liquid-metal dealloying to selectively replace Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels with Cu, producing a directionally aligned bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture and a spontaneous approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer. The generated answer instead proposes depositing a generic nanocrystalline RHEA coating at an existing W/Cu interface. Its mechanism omits selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V ligaments, W-rich passivation, and aligned Cu conduction pathways. Its operating conditions are vague and treat generic fusion irradiation as equivalent to the much narrower 25 keV He-ion screening used in the target. The experiment is reasonably discriminating, but should specify coating composition and thickness, thermal cycling, irradiation species/energy/fluence, statistical replication, and interface-resistance measurements. Most importantly, E1 validates irradiation tolerance of a separate WTaCrVHf RHEA, not the claimed thermal-conductivity benefit at a W–Cu interface.
